title: working on a social digital boardgame with Claude + rapid prototyping rawks
author: FetusCommander
selftext:
i've been working on this one for for a few months, but i think i've finally "found the fun" thanks to brainstorming with Claude.  this game, Posthuman Chess, started as a chess variant (i posted it initially to r/chessvariants, but by the time i did it had warped so far from chess that mods removed it, lol), and now it's basically some kind of homage to 1990s 4X, Dokapon Kingdom, and Scorched Earth with childhood friends.

  
one thing i'm enjoying a lot with AI is how painless it makes the part of design that lurks between first working mechanics build and locking in on system stuff.  for me, i think a big problem has always been that once i find a mechanic that excites me, i'm hesitant to pivot into different ways of exploring its implications because of sunk cost but also because the actual step of "change this game loop slightly several times until it captures the feeling i want" is a non-trivial burden to code.  AI has erased the preciousness/purity of mechanics for me and many times i now pivot into things that improve my overall happiness or experiential feeling with the design just by brainstorming thoughts that i would otherwise discard as too costly.

saying this isn't revolutionary, but in the face of the clone wars/NextFest "slop" debates, i think the use of AI has changed the way i value and experience novelty in games.  i've always been a social gamer and i think that the novelty of social experiences surrounding gaming is something that's hard to really emulate or "ripoff," because the vectors and variables and social contexts/social contracts for gaming are so personal.  i'm trying to figure out what to do with that thought, but yeah, having fun with this stuff
